title: Specification Mining from Lean Mathlib: Can LLMs Extract Safety-Relevant Specs from Existing Proofs?

original_idea.body:
# Specification Mining from Lean Mathlib: Can LLMs Extract Safety-Relevant Specs from Existing Proofs?

**Problem:** Lean's Mathlib contains thousands of formally proven theorems. Whether LLMs can mine these proofs to extract specification patterns relevant to security applications (boundedness, monotonicity, commutativity) is unstudied.

**Direction:** Sample 50 Mathlib theorems relevant to programming (sorting, arithmetic, data structures). Use LLMs to extract general specification patterns. Test whether these patterns transfer to new programs as starting specifications. Measure whether Mathlib-sourced specs lead to higher proof success rates than LLM-generated specs from scratch.

**Why it matters:** Mathlib is a vast, formally verified knowledge base. If it can be mined for reusable specification patterns, it provides a head start for security-critical formal verification without requiring new spec writing.

**Relevant context:** Mathlib has 100K+ theorems. CSLib will extend this to CS algorithms. Specification mining from Mathlib for new applications is not studied. This could significantly reduce spec writing overhead.
